founding_context: Created in 1983 by Maati Bouabid, a former UNFP/USFP figure who had served as Prime Minister from 1979 to 1983, in the run-up to the 1984 legislative elections. The party is generally classified by academic and encyclopaedic sources (Tafra, Wikipedia) as one of the 'administrative' parties formed with palace backing under Hassan II, and it came first in the 1984 (83 of 306 seats) and 1993 (54 of 333 seats) legislative elections.

founders: Parti de l'avant-garde démocratique et socialiste (PADS)
founding_context: Launched in 2014 as an electoral and political alliance of three small left-wing parties (PSU, PADS, CNI) that had boycotted the 2011 legislative election. It contested the 2015 local and 2016 legislative elections under a common banner, winning two seats in 2016 (Omar Balafrej and Nabila Mounib). In late 2022, after about eight years as a coalition, the PADS, the CNI and the 'Gauche unitaire' current (with the 'Alternative progressiste' and independent activists) dissolved themselves and merged into a single party carrying the FGD name; the PSU did not join the merger and remains a separate party.

founders: Fidélité à la démocratie (Mohamed Sassi, joined 2005)
founding_context: Created in July 2002 as the Gauche socialiste unifiée (GSU) by the merger of Mohamed Bensaid Aït Idder's OADP with several small left groups; it took the name Parti socialiste unifié in 2005 after absorbing the 'Fidélité à la démocratie' current led by Mohamed Sassi, a former USFP figure. The PSU positions itself as a democratic-socialist party critical of the constitutional balance of power; it boycotted the 2011 legislative election, then contested 2016 and 2021 within the FGD alliance. In January 2012 Nabila Mounib became its Secretary General, widely reported as the first woman to head a Moroccan political party.

founders: Former militants of the Marxist-Leninist organisation Ila al-Amam (incl. Abdellah El Harif)
founding_context: Founded in 1995 by former members of the clandestine Marxist-Leninist organisation 'Ila al-Amam' (of which it describes itself as the political and intellectual continuation); it was legally recognised only in 2004. founding_context: Left-wing split from the Istiqlal in September 1959 led by Mehdi Ben Barka, Abderrahim Bouabid and Abdellah Ibrahim, with the UMT trade union. In 1975 the Rabat wing under Bouabid became the USFP; the residual UNFP (Casablanca wing, Abdellah Ibrahim) boycotted elections and faded into inactivity.

names.fr: Front pour la défense des institutions constitutionnelles
names.en: Front for the Defence of Constitutional Institutions

founding_context: Palace-aligned electoral front created in 1963 by Ahmed Réda Guédira, a close adviser of Hassan II, to counter the Istiqlal and UNFP in the first legislative election; it grouped the Mouvement populaire, the Parti démocrate constitutionnel and independents. It won a plurality in 1963 and broke up within a few years; it is the archetype of the 'administrative party' in Moroccan political analysis.
